top_signal.title: Need advice about employee
top_signal.summary: I started my business just under seven years ago. It is a day spa offering lash, brow, wax, and skin services. Up until about three months ago, it had just been me wearing all the hats and doing all the services. I’ve been incredibly fortunate to grow enough that I was able to move into a storefront, expand our services, and hire estheticians.  I want my spa to be a good work environment for its staff, and I want both employees and clients to feel good about coming here. Unfortunately, I’m having a few issues with one employee, and I’m struggling to figure out whether these are normal growing pains with a new employee or signs that this simply isn’t a good fit.  During the interview process, she told me that she was newly moving to the area, fresh out of school, and has two young children at home whom she needs to be home with during the week. She was looking for a part-time position that worked with her partial SAHM schedule. I told her that wasn’t a problem, and we worked out a schedule that seemed to work for both of us.  She was hired to work Friday from 3:30 p.m.–8:00 p.m., plus Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m. I hired her at a 50/50 commission rate plus tips and told her that I’m very understanding when things come up—sick children, being out of town, family obligations, etc.—but that I needed to know about those things ahead of time and, whenever possible, before clients had been booked on her schedule for those days.
